name: How long does ground-up commercial construction take in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: How long does ground-up commercial construction usually take in Los Angeles for a small-to-mid size building?
mainEntity.text: How long does ground-up commercial construction usually take in Los Angeles for a small-to-mid size building?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ground-up commercial construction in Los Angeles usually takes longer than owners expect because the schedule is driven by several separate phases, not just field labor. A typical timeline often runs 12 to 24 months for small-to-mid size projects, but that range can expand if the site needs grading, demolition, utility relocations, entitlements, environmental review, or redesign after plan check comments. Design and permitting can take as long as construction itself on some projects. The best way to estimate duration is to break the project into phases: feasibility, concept design, approvals, permit issuance, procurement, sitework, structural build, MEP rough-in, inspections, and final closeout. In Los Angeles-area cities, inspection availability and utility coordination can add hidden delays. Owners should also account for long-lead materials, especially switchgear, HVAC equipment, and specialty glazing. A strong preconstruction plan should include a milestone schedule with allowance for city review cycles and contingency time. If the building has a specific tenant opening date, the schedule should be built backward from that date and include float for approvals. The most reliable contractors provide a realistic critical-path schedule rather than a best-case estimate.
acceptedAnswer.description: Most small-to-mid size ground-up commercial projects in Los Angeles take about 12 to 24 months from early design through certificate of occupancy, depending on site conditions, permitting, utility coordination, and inspection cycles. Projects with demolition, zoning issues, or tenant-specific requirements often take longer. A realistic schedule should include design, approvals, procurement, construction, inspections, and closeout.
